label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1012a2-4: Thought, in affirming or denying, is thereby true or false
interpretation: Reading B (universal), second half: 'whenever it is true or false' read not as a condition but as saying that thought, in affirming or denying any object, is thereby true or false. This is STMT-AFFIRMING-OR-DENYING-THOUGHT-IS-TRUE-OR-FALSE. Bivalence for thought, that every proposition is the object of some true or false thought (STMT-EVERY-OBJECT-OF-THOUGHT-JUDGED-TRULY-OR-FALSELY), adds the extension to every proposition and is not attributed to this sentence: it is the formalization's own open premise. The verified result ARIST-MET-1012A-THOUGHT-BIVALENCE-IFF-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE shows that, given readings A and the composition premise, this is equivalent to excluded middle, so on this reading the passage restates the law rather than arguing for it against someone who withholds it.
